subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Does a current-main Telegram run show that upgrading Pi to 0.80.4 removes the visible placeholder, or does OpenClaw still inject a synthetic display value after provider normalization?
rationale: The two outcomes have different owners and fixes: a dependency upgrade versus an OpenClaw reply/display boundary correction; source strings alone cannot establish which payload Telegram receives.

options.title: Capture both dependency paths
options.body: Record the redacted outbound Telegram payload on the current Pi pin and Pi 0.80.4 before authorizing code changes.

options.title: Narrow to Pi normalization
options.body: Track only the confirmed `(see attached image)` dependency path and require separate evidence before changing WebChat/transcript labels.
